Package com.github.jpmsilva.jsystemd.spring

Class FlywayStatusProvider

java.lang.Object
com.github.jpmsilva.jsystemd.spring.FlywayStatusProvider
All Implemented Interfaces:
StartingStatusProvider, StatusProvider, StoppingStatusProvider, FlywayConfigurationCustomizer, Ordered
public class FlywayStatusProvider extends Object implements StartingStatusProvider, StoppingStatusProvider, FlywayConfigurationCustomizer, Ordered
Implementation of StatusProvider that provides the progress of the Flyway database migrations run on startup, such as Flyway: applying migration 42 add index (41 applied).

The migrations are run by the Flyway instance that Spring Boot sets up, once it is created. This provider is a customizer of its configuration, which adds a Callback that reports each migration it applies, next to the callbacks it already has, such as the Callback beans of the application. Each migration also extends the startup timeout, as a migration of many versions can take longer than the TimeoutStartSec of the service unit; a single migration that takes longer than the timeout extension still exceeds it, in which case TimeoutStartSec must be raised.

The progress is reported through a PhaseStatusProvider of its own, sent to systemd right away on every change, and cleared once the migrations complete. When they fail, the migration that failed is still reported, while the application fails to start: it reports while the application starts up, and while it stops, as a StartingStatusProvider and a StoppingStatusProvider, as an application that fails to start goes straight from starting to stopping.

It is the last of the customizers to run, unless they are ordered otherwise, so that the callbacks they set are kept: a customizer that runs after it and sets the callbacks replaces the one of this provider, in which case the migrations are not reported. A Flyway instance that the application creates itself is not customized by Spring Boot: add the callback to its configuration with customize(FluentConfiguration).

Joao Silva
